articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr. gets the best possible news with Giants season opener nearing
articles.standfirst: The veteran wide receiver is hoping for a major bounce-back season with the franchise where his legend started.
articles.summary: The veteran wide receiver is hoping for a major bounce-back season with the franchise where his legend started.
articles.body:
There's a lot of hype surrounding the New York Giants heading into the 2026 NFL season. Rightfully so, as the team made shrewd additions to the roster in the offseason, have an ascending young quarterback in Jaxson Dart , and will now be coached by John Harbaugh .

Yet it's a former Giants superstar returning at 33 years old that may end up being the top storyline. Odell Beckham Jr. , who exploded onto the scene with the Giants in 2014 and made three Pro Bowls in New York, is back with the franchise for the 2026 season.

" OBJ " spent the entire 2025 season out of football, unable to latch on to a team before he was ultimately suspended for six games in October . That came after he failed to make an impact with the Baltimore Ravens and Miami Dolphins , all while never recovering his elite form due to a multitude of injuries .

John Harbaugh says OBJ is in the midst of his best week of camp so far

By all accounts, Beckham has looked like a completely different person this summer with the Giants . The reports have been extremely positive. On Wednesday, Harbaugh echoed that sentiment, making a bold claim about OBJ as the season nears.

I think Odell's had a good camp. I would say his best week of camp has come this week. He's looked good and made numerous plays. Just like you saw, even today he made numerous plays. So he's doing well.

Harbaugh hasn't assured anyone that Beckham is going to end up making the 53-man roster for the season. His chances certainly increased following the news that Calvin Austin tore his ACL and is out for the season .

OBJ, Isaiah Hodgins and Jalin Hyatt might be competing for one or two of the final wide receiver spots. Right now, it seems like Beckham has the upper hand.

articles.title: Cam Skattebo starts Giants practice brawl after reckless play nearly injures teammates
articles.standfirst: Cam Skattebo’s intensity is becoming a problem in the Giants’ locker room.
articles.summary: Cam Skattebo’s intensity is becoming a problem in the Giants’ locker room.
articles.body:
Cam Skattebo ’s energy is one of his defining traits, but it appears to be starting to become an issue inside the New York Giants locker room.

According to the latest reports, some of the running back’s teammates were reportedly unhappy with his actions during Wednesday’s practice, in an incident that even led to a confrontation within the team.

According to Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News , Skattebo “started a fight” after a reception in which he slid and came “dangerously close to taking out the legs of multiple defensive backs.” The reporter noted that Jevon Holland and Greg Newsome were among the players who expressed their frustration.

Leonard also suggested that the running back’s attitude “is starting to wear on his defensive teammates,” after Skattebo ran over linebacker Zaire Barnes during a previous practice despite the defense being prohibited from making contact.

Even head coach John Harbaugh addressed the incident when asked about Skattebo’s intensity.

“He got a 15-yard penalty at the end of practice,” Harbaugh said when asked about Skattebo’s infectious energy. “Did you see that? Yeah, it’s infectious. It can be infectious the other way, an infectious disease type of thing. We want it to be in a positive way.”

Skattebo has built a reputation for his physical running style, aggressive approach, and willingness to embrace contact on every play. The Giants are well aware of that personality and even appeared to embrace it last season, when they asked several teammates to imitate the way the running back plays.

However, bringing that intensity against his own defensive teammates or putting them at risk during non-contact practices can create friction inside the locker room.

The incident became significant enough that Harbaugh compared Skattebo’s energy to an “infectious disease,” a comment that quickly drew attention.

Fortunately for New York, the regular season is only a few weeks away. The Giants will open the 2026 campaign on September 13 against the Dallas Cowboys , giving Skattebo the opportunity to channel his aggression against opponents rather than his own teammates.

His return will be one of the major storylines to follow after his 2025 rookie season was limited to just eight games due to a fractured tibia and a dislocated ankle. If he can regain the form he showed before the injury, the Giants could have a dangerous offense alongside wide receiver Malik Nabers.

In eight games last season, Skattebo recorded 410 rushing yards, 207 receiving yards, and seven total touchdowns. According to Jordan Raanan of ESPN, he was also listed as the team’s starting running back on the unofficial depth chart ahead of the preseason finale against the New York Jets .

The decision reflects the team’s confidence that he is fully recovered and ready to contribute, although for now, his intensity appears to have created some issues inside his own locker room.

articles.title: Darius Slayton’s $36 million contract may not save him as Giants face brutal decision after seven years
articles.standfirst: The longest-tenured player on the Giants suddenly finds himself fighting for something that once seemed almost guaranteed
articles.summary: The longest-tenured player on the Giants suddenly finds himself fighting for something that once seemed almost guaranteed
articles.body:
For seven seasons, Darius Slayton survived just about every kind of change the New York Giants could throw at him. Different quarterbacks, different coaches, losing seasons, playoff football and even previous battles for his own roster spot. Through all of it, the wide receiver remained.

Now, with a $36 million contract and more time in a Giants uniform than anyone else currently on the roster, Slayton could be approaching the end of his run in New York.

The Giants are reportedly seriously considering releasing the 29-year-old as they prepare to trim their roster to 53 players by Sunday's 6 p.m. ET deadline . And perhaps the most telling sign came Friday night against the Jets. While John Harbaugh protected most players whose jobs appeared secure , Slayton started and remained on the field deep into the preseason finale, playing 33 offensive snaps even after Jameis Winston gave way to third-string quarterback Brandon Allen. He finished the night without a catch or even a target.

After seven years, Slayton could be playing his final days as a Giant

That would have been difficult to imagine when Slayton signed a three-year, $36 million deal to remain with New York last year. But money may not be enough to protect him. He is due more than $12 million in salary this season, with $9.75 million fully guaranteed, and releasing him would leave the Giants carrying roughly $12.75 million in dead money for 2026. New York would save only around $3.2 million in cap space.

Slayton underwent sports hernia surgery after catching only 37 passes in 14 games last season and has not consistently looked like his old self this summer. There was a glimpse of it against Miami, when he caught four passes for 58 yards and finally produced the kind of performance Harbaugh said he “needed to see.” But one week later, Slayton played extensive snaps against the Jets and disappeared from the stat sheet.

And then there is Odell Beckham Jr. On the same night Slayton went without a target, Beckham also played 33 snaps but caught three passes for 53 yards and continued making his own case to survive the final cuts.

Harbaugh said afterward that Beckham had done enough to make “an NFL roster,” stopping short of promising that roster would be New York's. The season-ending ACL injury suffered by Calvin Austin III created another opening in a suddenly complicated receiver room, but it still may not be enough to guarantee Slayton's place.

Slayton has spent his entire NFL career in New York. The Giants drafted him in the fifth round in 2019, and seven years later he has played 106 games and made 78 starts for the team. No player currently on the roster has been a Giant longer. Just last year, the team gave him a new three-year, $36 million contract. Now, less than 18 months later, he is waiting to find out if his time in New York is over. The Giants have until Sunday evening to make that decision.

articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr's first words and message to Giants fans after earning his way onto final 53-man roster
articles.standfirst: OBJ came back to New York with nothing to lose, and John Harbaugh rewarded his hard work.
articles.summary: OBJ came back to New York with nothing to lose, and John Harbaugh rewarded his hard work.
articles.body:
When Odell Beckham Jr. signed with the New York Giants this summer, it was an emotional moment for him and for Giants fans who loved him during his first stint with the franchise. But OBJ had a tough hill to climb.

At 33 years old with various injuries sapping his otherworldly athleticism, Beckham was far from a lock to make the final 53-man roster. He also had plenty of competition in the wide receiver room. Malik Nabers , Darnell Mooney , Malachi Fields , and Darius Slayton were practically locked into the top four depth chart spots. But everything broke right for Beckham.

Free agent signing Calvin Austin III suffered a season-ending injury, paving the way for OBJ to compete with Jalin Hyatt and Isaiah Hodgins for one roster spot. On Sunday, Beckham won out, with head coach John Harbaugh opting to keep the veteran onboard over the other two.

Odell Beckham Jr. had a very strong training camp and grinded his way to a roster spot

Harbaugh spoke consistently this past week about what a great camp Beckham had. He earned his spot on the team the old-fashioned way . And once he did, OBJ made sure to leave Giants fans with a hopeful message, via Josina Anderson .

I am excited. I found out when I was walking off the field. Coach [Harbaugh] said congratulations and he said that I worked hard. I told him I will give him everything I got. He said, 'Let’s go do it'. After that I went to the locker room and I just dapped up my teammates. Jameis (Winston) definitely gave love and so did Jaxson (Dart). Everybody gave me love. Now I just got to go get it. I have one more gear to go; one more gear in me. I came to New York to give my all, and that's what they’re going to get out of me. To the city, to the fans, I love you.

It's unclear at this point in time what kind of role Harbaugh and offensive coordinator Matt Nagy envision for Beckham. One would expect a very part-time role for OBJ to start, but if his strong training camp continues into the preseason, his role could expand rather quickly.

articles.title: Back in Blue and 13: Odell Beckham Jr. officially switches jersey numbers ahead of season opener
articles.standfirst: The veteran wide receiver is returning to the number that became synonymous with his explosive rise in New York
articles.summary: The veteran wide receiver is returning to the number that became synonymous with his explosive rise in New York
articles.body:
O dell Beckham Jr.’ s comeback with the New York Giants now has an even more familiar look.

Just days after securing a place on the Giants ’ initial 53-man roster, Beckham is officially reclaiming the No. 13 jersey, the number he wore throughout the first five seasons of his NFL career and during the period when he established himself as one of the league’s biggest stars.

The Giants announced the change Tuesday, completing a return that has already carried plenty of nostalgia for the 33-year-old receiver.

The timing is particularly fitting. Beckham had been wearing No. 3 throughout training camp and the preseason after returning to the Giants, while No. 13 belonged to Jalin Hyatt.

Even after Beckham was informed that he had made the roster, he was still wearing No. 3 at Monday’s practice. However, Beckham had already hinted that a switch could be coming.

Asked Monday about the possibility of getting his old number back, Beckham said: “I think we all know what that means to me, and there definitely will be some conversations. I'll just say we'll see what happens, but like I said, it would be an honor and a privilege to put that back on.”

Those conversations have now produced the outcome Giants fans were hoping for.

Hyatt, who was released as part of the Giants ’ roster cuts before subsequently returning to the practice squad, has moved from No. 13 to No. 81. That opened the door for Beckham to officially step back into the jersey that became one of the most recognizable in Giants history.

No. 13 carries a huge part of Beckham's Giants legacy

Beckham’s connection with the number goes far beyond simply wearing it early in his career.

The Giants selected him No. 12 overall in the 2014 NFL Draft, and although he missed the opening portion of his rookie season, he quickly became one of the league’s most spectacular offensive weapons.

His one-handed catch against the Dallas Cowboys that season became an enduring NFL highlight, while his production earned him three Pro Bowl selections during his original spell in New York.

Across 59 games from 2014 through 2018, Beckham caught 390 passes for 5,476 yards and 44 touchdowns. Those numbers still rank him second in franchise history in receiving yards and fourth in both receptions and receiving touchdowns.

After leaving New York, Beckham continued wearing No. 13 with the Cleveland Browns. But when he joined the Los Angeles Rams during the 2021 season, he changed to No. 3, the number he subsequently kept with the Baltimore Ravens and Miami Dolphins .

The No. 3 jersey also became associated with a major achievement in Beckham’s career. With the Rams, he helped the team win Super Bowl LVI, catching 21 passes for 288 yards and two touchdowns during Los Angeles’ postseason run before a knee injury ended his night in the championship game.

Now, however, it is No. 13 that will be on Beckham’s back when he takes the field for the Giants again.

That comeback is significant in its own right. Beckham spent the entire 2025 season out of the NFL before returning to New York this offseason.

He then had to compete for a roster spot under new head coach John Harbaugh, ultimately earning his place after a productive preseason. Beckham caught seven passes for 76 yards on 13 targets across three preseason appearances.

The Giants will begin the regular season at home against the Dallas Cowboys on Sept. 13, meaning Beckham’s first official game back in New York will come against a familiar NFC East opponent.

Whether he can reproduce the numbers or explosive plays that defined his first Giants tenure remains to be seen.

His role is also likely to be managed carefully as the coaching staff works him into an offense featuring Malik Nabers, Darnell Mooney, Darius Slayton and rookie Malachi Fields.

But visually, at least, the circle is now complete.

Beckham is back with the Giants, back in blue and, finally, back in No. 13. For supporters who still have his original jersey tucked away, there is now a very good reason to bring it out again.

articles.title: From a dark place to Week 1: How Cam Skattebo overcame a serious injury and dark thoughts to avoid retirement
articles.standfirst: The Giants running back has gone from a devastating rookie-season setback to preparing for his return against Dallas
articles.summary: The Giants running back has gone from a devastating rookie-season setback to preparing for his return against Dallas
articles.body:
C am Skattebo 's first NFL season ended so abruptly that the New York Giants running back found himself questioning whether he wanted to play football at all.

A fourth-round pick out of Arizona State in the 2025 NFL Draft, Skattebo had quickly become one of the most exciting young players in New York before a devastating injury against the Philadelphia Eagles brought his rookie campaign to an early conclusion.

Now, nearly a year later, Skattebo is preparing for the 2026 season and expects to be available when the Giants open their campaign against the Dallas Cowboys on Sept. 13.

The journey back has involved considerably more than physical rehabilitation.

Skattebo suffered a dislocated right ankle and a broken right fibula during New York's Week 8 matchup with Philadelphia on Oct. 26, 2025. His leg became trapped awkwardly underneath him during a tackle, leaving him needing immediate medical attention before he was taken to a Philadelphia hospital and underwent surgery.

The timing made the injury particularly difficult. Skattebo had already established himself as an important part of the Giants' offense, rushing for 410 yards and five touchdowns while adding 207 receiving yards and two touchdown catches through eight games.

He had also delivered a memorable three-touchdown performance against the Eagles just two weeks before suffering the injury. But the physical damage was only part of the battle.

Skattebo revealed this week that he had entered professional football with a very specific personal rule. If he suffered a major injury, he planned to walk away from the game.

"Coming out of college, going into the NFL, I think I gave myself one rule, and it was if I ever got a major injury, I was done playing," he told Kay Adams on ‘Up and Adams’. "And that happened seven games into my career, so it kind of sucked."

For a player who had only just reached the NFL, the prospect of having his career effectively stopped almost immediately was difficult to process.

The injury also forced Skattebo into a prolonged period away from the environment that had defined his life. Instead of preparing for games, competing for carries and developing alongside quarterback Jaxson Dart, he was facing surgery, rehabilitation and months of uncertainty.

That time away ultimately became an important part of his decision to continue.

The mental battle became as important as the physical recovery

Skattebo has been open about how difficult the recovery became mentally. During the interview, he acknowledged that retirement was not merely a passing thought.

"I would say probably a month in," he continued. "Like the first month was kind of like, 'Do I really wanna do this?' And then, you know, I got to go back and play."

That decision changed the direction of his career.

Rather than allowing the injury to define his future, Skattebo began working toward a return. By January, he was already telling the Giants that the setback would not prevent him from continuing.

The organization also remained encouraged by his progress as he worked his way through rehabilitation.

The road was not straightforward. Skattebo explained during the offseason that the psychological side of returning to football was sometimes more difficult than the physical work itself.

"Obviously, there’s ups and downs in the injury process and coming back and rehabbing, but the mental battle has been the hardest part: making sure that I trust it fully," Skattebo said in May. Still, his confidence continued to grow.

In May, Skattebo told Giants fans that he expected to be ready for Week 1. That target has now become increasingly realistic, with the running back appearing for New York during the preseason as he continued to test his surgically repaired ankle.

His return also comes at an important moment for the Giants. New York has undergone significant changes, including the arrival of head coach John Harbaugh , while Skattebo is expected to compete for touches in a running back room that includes veteran Najee Harris, Tyrone Tracy Jr. and Devin Singletary . There is also unfinished business for Skattebo personally.

Before the injury, he had emerged as a key part of the Giants' young offensive core alongside Dart. His physical running style, receiving ability and personality quickly made him a fan favorite, but he has insisted that popularity only matters if it eventually translates into winning.

The next step is therefore not simply proving that his ankle can withstand an NFL game.

Skattebo once believed a major injury would automatically mean retirement. Seven games into his NFL career, that exact scenario arrived. He came close to walking away, but the months that followed forced him to confront a different version of himself.

And when the Giants line up against Dallas in Week 1, Skattebo will not simply be coming back from a broken leg and dislocated ankle. He will be returning after overcoming the possibility that he might never want to play football again.

"Coming out of college, going into the NFL, I think I gave myself one rule, and it was if I ever got a major injury, I was done playing," he told Kay Adams on ‘Up and Adams’. "And that happened seven games into my career, so it kind of sucked."
For a player who had only just reached the NFL, the prospect of having his career effectively stopped almost immediately was difficult to process.

The injury also forced Skattebo into a prolonged period away from the environment that had defined his life. Instead of preparing for games, competing for carries and developing alongside quarterback Jaxson Dart, he was facing surgery, rehabilitation and months of uncertainty.
That time away ultimately became an important part of his decision to continue.
The mental battle became as important as the physical recovery
Skattebo has been open about how difficult the recovery became mentally. During the interview, he acknowledged that retirement was not merely a passing thought.
"I would say probably a month in," he continued. "Like the first month was kind of like, 'Do I really wanna do this?' And then, you know, I got to go back and play."
That decision changed the direction of his career.
Rather than allowing the injury to define his future, Skattebo began working toward a return. By January, he was already telling the Giants that the setback would not prevent him from continuing.
The organization also remained encouraged by his progress as he worked his way through rehabilitation.
The road was not straightforward. Skattebo explained during the offseason that the psychological side of returning to football was sometimes more difficult than the physical work itself.

"Obviously, there’s ups and downs in the injury process and coming back and rehabbing, but the mental battle has been the hardest part: making sure that I trust it fully," Skattebo said in May. Still, his confidence continued to grow.

In May, Skattebo told Giants fans that he expected to be ready for Week 1. That target has now become increasingly realistic, with the running back appearing for New York during the preseason as he continued to test his surgically repaired ankle.

His return also comes at an important moment for the Giants. New York has undergone significant changes, including the arrival of head coach John Harbaugh , while Skattebo is expected to compete for touches in a running back room that includes veteran Najee Harris, Tyrone Tracy Jr. and Devin Singletary . There is also unfinished business for Skattebo personally.

Before the injury, he had emerged as a key part of the Giants' young offensive core alongside Dart. His physical running style, receiving ability and personality quickly made him a fan favorite, but he has insisted that popularity only matters if it eventually translates into winning.
The next step is therefore not simply proving that his ankle can withstand an NFL game.

Skattebo once believed a major injury would automatically mean retirement. Seven games into his NFL career, that exact scenario arrived. He came close to walking away, but the months that followed forced him to confront a different version of himself.

And when the Giants line up against Dallas in Week 1, Skattebo will not simply be coming back from a broken leg and dislocated ankle. He will be returning after overcoming the possibility that he might never want to play football again.

articles.title: Arthur Marshall Cause of Death: Former Giants and Broncos receiver dies at 57
articles.summary: Arthur Marshall, the former NFL receiver whose unlikely path to the league included one of the most unusual touchdown passes of his era, has died at 57 after a battle with stomach cancer.
articles.body:
Arthur Marshall , the former NFL receiver whose unlikely path to the league included one of the most unusual touchdown passes of his era, has died at 57 after a battle with stomach cancer.

Marshall , who spent five seasons in the NFL with the Denver Broncos and New York Giants , died Wednesday. His death prompted tributes in his native Georgia, where he first emerged as a standout athlete before eventually reaching the professional ranks.

His obituary remembered a man whose impact stretched well beyond football.

“A former professional NFL athlete, Arthur carried strength and determination throughout his life,” it read. “But those who knew him best will remember him most for the size of his heart.

"He was a giver by nature-generous with his time, love, encouragement, and support. He genuinely cared for people and found joy in helping others.”

Marshall grew up in Hephzibah, Georgia, before playing college football for the Georgia Bulldogs from 1988 through 1991. He averaged 17.7 yards per reception during his college career but wasn't selected in the 1992 NFL Draft.

Denver gave him his opportunity as an undrafted free agent, and Marshall quickly showed why he belonged.

One throw and a place in NFL record book

Marshall ’s most memorable moment came during his rookie season against the Dallas Cowboys in December 1992.

On a trick play, the receiver threw an 81-yard touchdown pass to Cedric Tillman , tying the NFL record at the time for the longest touchdown completion by a non-quarterback.

The score briefly put Denver ahead of a Dallas team led by Troy Aikman before the Cowboys eventually won. Marshall was far more than a gadget-play option during his two seasons with the Broncos .

He caught 54 passes for 853 yards and three touchdowns while also contributing in the return game. Remarkably, he finished his Denver tenure having thrown two touchdown passes of his own.

The Broncos traded him to the Giants before the 1994 season. Marshall spent his final three NFL campaigns in New York, recording another 414 receiving yards and a touchdown while continuing to work on special teams.

He finished his career with 87 receptions for 1,267 yards, four receiving touchdowns and 2,303 all-purpose yards.

The player who made it out

Marshall ’s rise from a small Georgia community to the NFL remained a source of pride at Hephzibah High School , which inducted him into its Hall of Fame in 2003.

“When he touched the field, you knew he was on the field,” current Hephzibah coach Daniel Dorsey told Fox 54. “He made a difference, whether it was offense, defense or special teams. He was just a special player all around.”

Dorsey said Marshall ’s progression from Hephzibah to Georgia and eventually the NFL “speaks volumes to who he is and the mountains that you can climb if you just put your mind to it.”

Marshall ’s post-playing life included a federal bank fraud case. He pleaded guilty to two counts and was sentenced in 2010 to 69 months in prison, along with five years of supervised release and more than $3.6 million in restitution.

His football story, however, remains defined by persistence as an undrafted player who fought his way onto an NFL roster, became a productive receiver and produced a record-tying play that remains part of his legacy.

articles.title: NFL’s newest power couple Jaxson Dart and Marissa Ayers share loved-up TikTok: 'We're obsessed with each other'
articles.standfirst: Dart and Ayers showcase their close bond as the quarterback prepares for his sophmore season
articles.summary: Dart and Ayers showcase their close bond as the quarterback prepares for his sophmore season
articles.body:
New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart and Marissa Ayers are giving fans another glimpse into their increasingly public romance, with the couple appearing together in a playful TikTok ahead of the 2026 NFL season.

Ayers shared a clip showing herself and Dart dancing together, adding a caption that described their relationship as spending “everyday” together because they’re “obsessed” with one another.

She followed it with the caption, “idc that's my bestie,” offering another affectionate snapshot of their relationship and showing the dynamic they share away from the football field.

The post comes as Dart prepares for his second NFL campaign, while Ayers continues building her own profile as a model and social media influencer. The pair's relationship began in October 2025 and quickly attracted attention as their appearances together became more frequent.

Ayers has also found herself in the spotlight independently. She gained significant attention after appearing as a ring girl for the Anthony Joshua-Jake Paul fight, while her social media following has continued to grow.

Since getting together with Dart , she's regularly offered glimpses of their life as a couple.

Their romance has remained a regular feature of their social media presence. Ayers has supported Dart around the Giants, including appearances during training camp and at his youth football camp, while Dart has publicly championed her career.

She has also worked on modeling projects connected to the Giants, creating another link between her professional work and Dart's football world.

Romance grows as Dart eyes NFL leap

Dart has previously spoken warmly about Ayers , praising the independence they both have in their careers while emphasizing that they support each other's ambitions.

“It's really cool when you have two people who are independent what they do, but at the same time... are each other's biggest cheerleaders. She's amazing and she's going to do amazing things, so I can't wait to support her,” said Dart .

Their relationship has developed alongside an important stage in Dart's football journey. The 2025 first-round pick showed plenty of promise during his rookie season, completing 63.7 percent of his passes for 2,272 yards, 15 touchdowns and five interceptions. He also made a significant impact with his legs, rushing for 487 yards and nine touchdowns.

However, Dart's first season wasn't without setbacks. He dealt with injuries and underwent multiple concussion evaluations, making his durability one of the issues to watch as he enters his sophomore campaign.

Now, expectations are rising around the young quarterback. He's learning a new offensive system under the Giants' revamped coaching staff, led by head coach John Harbaugh, and has expressed confidence in his progress during training camp.

Dart has praised Harbaugh's intensity and passion for football, while acknowledging that the Giants still have plenty of work to do as they adjust to the new system. The quarterback believes he's more comfortable and in command than he was during the offseason.

With the new season approaching, Dart will be hoping that improved familiarity translates into stronger performances on Sundays. Away from the field, meanwhile, he appears to have a strong source of support in Ayers .

articles.title: Cam Skattebo and dog Duke are stars of new, landmark NFL partnership unveiled before season opener
articles.standfirst: The Giants star is helping launch new partnership that will extend across the Super Bowl and NFL Draft
articles.summary: The Giants star is helping launch new partnership that will extend across the Super Bowl and NFL Draft
articles.body:
The NFL is entering the 2026 season with a first-of-its-kind commercial partnership that reaches well beyond the football field.

The league announced a multi-year agreement with The Farmer’s Dog , naming the company its first-ever Official Pet Food Partner.

The partnership will be introduced through a campaign built around New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo and his senior rescue dog, Duke.

Skattebo’s involvement isn't simply the result of a new endorsement. He said Duke has been part of his life long before his NFL career began, and the two were already customers of The Farmer’s Dog .

“I’ve had Duke for every high and every low,” Skattebo said. “He’s been my teammate long before football became my career. I started feeding him The Farmer’s Dog because I wanted as many healthy years with him as possible.”

The campaign also includes Skattebo ’s Dachshund puppies, Cheech and Daizy , while focusing on the quieter parts of his life away from football, from travel and recovery to the routines he shares with his dogs.

Deal will stretch across NFL calendar

The partnership is designed to extend well beyond advertising around regular-season games.

The Farmer’s Dog is expected to appear around major league events including Super Bowl LXI, the NFL Combine and the NFL Draft. It will also connect with community programs such as My Cause My Cleats, Salute to Service and NFL FLAG.

Tracie Rodburg , the NFL’s senior vice president of global partnerships, said the relationship between fans and their dogs offered the league a natural way to broaden its partnerships.

“The NFL is all about bringing people together through shared experiences and community,” Rodburg said.

“Dogs are an important part of many families, and as the Official Pet Food Partner, The Farmer’s Dog will help us celebrate the role they play in our lives and communities throughout the season.”

The Farmer’s Dog already has a foothold in the league through its existing relationship with the Dallas Cowboys and Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders .

Its wider roster of partners also includes NASCAR champion Ryan Blaney , tennis player Jessica Pegula and The Oprah Podcast.

NFL’s newest category gets personal face

Skattebo ’s role gives the partnership an immediate connection to an active NFL player rather than relying only on league branding.

He said the opportunity also gives him a chance to encourage fans to think more carefully about their dogs’ health.

“If The Farmer’s Dog teaming up with the NFL gets even one more person thinking differently about what they feed their dog, that’s something I’m proud to be part of,” Skattebo said.

Jonathan Regev , CEO and co-founder of The Farmer’s Dog , linked that message directly to the culture surrounding elite athletes.

“We understand more than ever how much what we eat impacts our health and performance,” Regev said. “NFL players live that every day, and people increasingly recognize the same is true for their dogs.”

The announcement comes just as the NFL turns fully toward Week 1, but the timing also gives the league one final off-field headline before the games begin.

The 2026 season will start with a new sponsor, a new category and a campaign built around one of football’s more unexpected partnerships.
